---
title: "Presets"
subtitle: "One key for colours, fonts, style and motif in every format."
description: "The four presets of the mcanouil extension, how to select one, how a _brand.yml file changes it, the light and dark schemes, and the contrast check."
---

## Select a preset

Set the preset once, in the front matter or in `_quarto.yml`.
The same preset applies to `mcanouil-html`, `mcanouil-typst` and `mcanouil-revealjs`.

```yaml
extensions:
  mcanouil:
    preset: mono
```

The default preset is `gold`.

| Preset | Look | Fonts | Motif |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gold` | Editorial: small capitals, gilded rules, warm boxes with a thin gold edge. | Source Serif 4, Fira Code | Facets |
| `mono` | Swiss: graphite on white, blue links, upper case H2 under a rule, square corners. | Alegreya Sans, Fira Code | Steps |
| `quarto` | Documentation: pill tags, callouts framed in their colour, an accent bar beside headings. | Alegreya Sans, Fira Code | Ribbon |
| `terminal` | Console: a `$` prompt on titles, `[ ]` around kickers, dashed callout frames. Dark only. | JetBrains Mono | Dot field |

: The four presets. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[14,50,22,14]"}

The extension ships the fonts as files.
HTML, Reveal.js and Typst all use the same files, so the output does not change offline and no request goes to a font service.

Each preset has one corner motif.
The motif shows only on surfaces without a header or a footer in that corner: covers, chapter dividers, memo banners, the HTML title block, and the title, section and closing slides.
The motif never sits under text.
It is an artefact in the PDF tags and `aria-hidden` in HTML, and forced colours mode removes it.

## Light and dark

- HTML follows the light or dark setting of the reader.
- Reveal.js is light by default.
  Title, section and closing slides always use the dark ground of the preset.
- Typst is light by default.

Set `brand-mode: dark` for a dark PDF or a dark deck:

```yaml
brand-mode: dark
```

`terminal` is dark only, in every format.
If you request the light scheme with `terminal`, the render ignores the request and gives a warning.

## Change a preset with `_brand.yml`

A `_brand.yml` file in the project changes the preset.
Each value that the brand sets replaces the preset value.
The preset gives all the other values.

| Brand colour | Preset token |
| --- | --- |
| `primary` | `accent` |
| `background` | `paper` |
| `foreground` | `ink` |
| a token name, for example `link` or `muted` | that token |

: How the colours of `_brand.yml` replace the preset tokens. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[50,50]"}

```{.yaml filename="_brand.yml"}
color:
  primary: "#1b6b4a"
typography:
  base: Alegreya Sans
```

The brand fonts (`base`, `headings`, `monospace`) and the brand logo also replace the preset values.
A brand logo without alt text gives a warning.

## Contrast check

At each render, the extension measures every colour pair that the layouts use, in the light and the dark scheme.
The thresholds are those of WCAG 2.2 AA:

- 4.5:1 for text, for example ink on paper, links, muted text, and callout text on its tint.
- 3:1 for marks that are not text, for example rules, edges and focus rings.

If a pair is below its threshold, the render stops.
The message gives the pair, the two colours, the ratio and the threshold.
The extension does not correct your colours.
The preset colours pass in every scheme.

::: {.callout-caution}

The contrast check reads the tokens only.
Callout and pill backgrounds mix a small part of the type colour into the paper, so they are not tokens.
If your brand sets a semantic colour that is very near the paper, the tint of a callout can be too near the page.
Look at your callouts in both schemes after you change those colours.

:::
